subject: paper:volkow-2011
quote: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is typically characterized as a disorder of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity but there is increasing evidence of deficits in motivation.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes motivation as a third dimension of ADHD beyond the classic two — the mechanism this note names.

subject: paper:volkow-2011
quote: Using positron emission tomography (PET), we showed decreased function in the brain dopamine reward pathway in adults with ADHD, which, we hypothesized, could underlie the motivation deficits in this disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Direct neurobiological evidence tying a motivation deficit to reduced dopamine reward-pathway function in adults with ADHD.

subject: paper:luman-2005
quote: One of the core deficits in attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (AD/HD) is thought to be an aberrant sensitivity to reinforcement, such as reward and response cost.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. States the reinforcement-sensitivity account as a core-deficit candidate — the behavioural side of the reward story.

subject: paper:luman-2005
quote: Results indicate that reinforcement contingencies have a positive impact on task performance and levels of motivation for both children with AD/HD and normal controls. There is evidence that the effect related to task performance is somewhat more prominent in AD/HD.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Reward improves performance and motivation, somewhat more so in ADHD — the empirical basis for treating performance as contingency-dependent.

subject: paper:luman-2005
quote: Children with AD/HD prefer immediate over delayed reward.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Connects the note to the existing delay-aversion mechanism — the timing side of altered reward processing.

subject: paper:morsink-2017
quote: Individuals with ADHD appear to respond differently to incentives than their peers. This could be due to a general altered sensitivity to reinforcers.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Qualitative evidence that incentive response differs in ADHD; medium confidence as the study is interview-based and the theme structure was largely shared across groups.
